{"reconstruction": "WHAT THE PAGE IS. The title reads 'Fractionum communium per fractiones decimales expressarum periodi', i.e. 'Periods of common fractions expressed as decimal fractions'. For each prime denominator p from 3 to 83 the page gives two things.

(a) THE PERIODS. Let e = ord_p(10) and f = (p-1)/e. Gauss writes out the f distinct decimal periods, one for each coset of <10> in (Z/p)^*. After each period he repeats its first digit (e.g. '0 76923 0', '4 615384'), so a period can be read cyclically from any starting point.
- If 10 is a primitive root (f = 1), only the period of 1/p is given. This is the case for p = 7, 17, 19, 23, 29, 47, 59, 61.
- If f = 2, he gives 1/p and a second period. The second periods are 6/13, 17/31, 26/43, 12/67, 62/71 and 50/83.
- Larger f: for 11 (f = 5) the periods 09, 18, 36, 72, 45 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 5 over 11.
- For 37 (f = 12) the periods are 027, 351, 567, 378, 918, 945, 297, 864, 243, 162, 108, 405. These are r/37 for r = 1, 13, 21, 14, 34, 35, 11, 32, 9, 6, 4, 15.
- For 41 (f = 8; one row is cancelled) the periods are 1, 13, 5, 24, 25, 38, 2, 26 over 41.
- For 53 (f = 4) they are 1, 26, 40, 33 over 53.
- For 73 (f = 9) they are 1, 20, 35, 43, 57, 45, 24, 42, 37 over 73.
- For 79 (f = 6) they are 1, 29, 51, 57, 73, 63 over 79.
- For 3 and 5 the expansions are trivial ('033 066'; '2.4.6.8').
